title: Will Raised Earnings Guidance Change UnitedHealth Stock's Narrative - Simply Wall Street
content:
To own UnitedHealth Group, you need to believe the business can keep tightening operations faster than medical costs and legal pressure erode profitability. The latest quarter fits that story. Revenue was broadly flat year on year at US$112.7b, while net income reached US$4.1b and full year EPS guidance moved to at least US$19.50. The key near term swing factor is whether commercial, Medicare and Medicaid medical trends co operate enough for margin repair to stick. The biggest risk is still elevated medical costs and weak Medicaid margins, which could offset efficiency gains from AI programs and value based care in UnitedHealthcare and Optum. The most relevant fresh data point is the raised 2026 earnings outlook. Management now targets more than US$17.65b in net income and at least US$19.50 in diluted EPS. That guidance leans on tighter medical cost control, better Optum profitability and back office automation rather than volume expansion. For you as a shareholder, that update puts execution in the spotlight. If AI driven savings, value based care initiatives and Optum Health’s margin work stay on track, the guidance appears supported. If commercial and Medicaid cost trends stay stubbornly high, that same guidance could become harder to defend and the margin recovery narrative weakens. UnitedHealth Group's narrative projects US$502.0b revenue and US$23.5b earnings by 2029. This assumes 3.7% yearly revenue growth and an earnings increase of about US$9.4b from the current US$14.1b base. content: U.S. stock futures were mixed early Tuesday as Wall Street financial institutions officially kick off the third-quarter earnings season and traders digested turbulence in artificial intelligence (AI) and semiconductor stocks. JPMorgan Chase (JPM), Goldman Sachs (GS), Citigroup (C), and Wells Fargo (WFC), along with UnitedHealth and J&J, report before the bell today. As of 4:00 a.m. ET, Nasdaq futures fell 0.6%, S&P 500 futures were down 0.1%, while Dow futures rose 0.6% and Russell 2000 futures gained 0.5%. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), which tracks the S&P 500 Index, and Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ), which tracks the Nasdaq-100 Index, remained ‘bullish’. Noted investor Michael Burry flagged that the market could be setting up for a “bull trap” and added that he is holding back from adding any fresh bearish positions at current levels. Memory (MU, TSM, SKHY) and semiconductor stocks (NVDA, INTC, SNDK, AMD) extended the selloff in early premarket trading after capital-expenditure warnings from industry leaders and emerging competition from China’s CXMT. Broadcom (AVGO) CEO Hock Tan cautioned that access to capital could become a bigger bottleneck for AI infrastructure compared to chip or power availability. Intel CEO Lip Bu-Tan also raised questions recently about borrowing costs and the return on AI investments. In Korea, Samsung and SK Hynix dragged the KOSPI down over 6% on Tuesday. The Direxion Daily South Korea Bull 3X Shares (KORU ETF) cracked over 10% in early U.S. premarket trade. Nvidia (NVDA): Reports citing IDC data show Nvidia’s share of China’s data-center AI chip market fell to 34% in the first half of 2026 as Huawei gained ground. Navitas Semiconductor (NVTS) shares rose over 1% in early premarket trade after the company unveiled a 24kW power delivery board developed with Nvidia to target improved efficiency in AI racks. Optical networking stocks (COHR, LITE, AAOI) continued to fall in early premarket trade amid concerns over AI funding. However, retail traders on Stocktwits remained bullish and saw the dip as a buying opportunity. Meta Platforms (META): Its Muse AI retention data and traction drew a “monster long” call from Jim Cramer, while Dan Ives continued to make a bullish case, citing its competitive AI edge. Apple (AAPL) remains on the retail radar after a Bank of America note flagged shorter wait times for iPhone 18 Pro delivery than last year. Investors are also watching iPhone Duo pre-orders, scheduled to open on Friday. Cerebras (CBRS) shares continued to decline in early premarket trading, hitting a new 52-week low amid concerns about its relationship with OpenAI and an upcoming lockup expiring Wednesday. SpaceX (SPCX) launched 27 Starlink broadband satellites late on Monday, its first such mission in over three weeks. AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) remains on the retail radar even as an analyst flagged competitive risks from Starlink’s spectrum ambitions. They said SpaceX could build a “massive” midband spectrum by combining Ligand, Viasat-related spectrum access, and licenses from a proposed FCC auction. Telecom stocks (TMUS, VZ): Analysts have said that fears from SpaceX’s $8 billion spectrum deal to T-Mobile are ‘overblown’. Morningstar added that while the Starlink deal does raise uncertainty for wireless carriers, it is unlikely to threaten their operations. Tesla (TSLA) will be showcasing its Cybercab robotaxi at the Paris Motor Show this week, along with an Optimus robot and free FSD test drives. UnitedHealth Group (UNH) is trending on Stocktwits ahead of earnings today, with options market pricing in a 6.5% elevated move and analysts flagging high implied volatility. Six Flags Entertainment (FUN) shares fell 13% in early premarket trade following news of a guest fatality on the Goliath roller coaster at Six Flags in Georgia. Visa (V) shares rose over 1% in early premarket trading after China gave it the green light to begin preparing for a domestic bank-card clearing business, after years of regulatory hurdles. Other tickers trending on Stocktwits at the time of writing included Netflix (NFLX), Nuscale Power (SMR), Palantir (PLTR), and First Solar (FSLR). On the economic front, traders will tune in throughout the day for speeches from Fed Governor Christopher Waller, Richmond Fed President Thomas Barkin, and Boston Fed President Susan Collins. Meanwhile, on Monday, Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said that additional tightening may be required to return inflation to the Fed’s 2% target. This comes ahead of key inflation data (September CPI on Wednesday and PPI on Thursday) and Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s speech later in the week. Existing home sales data will be released at 10:00 am ET today. On the earnings front, watch out for JPMorgan Chase (JPM), UnitedHealth (UNH), Wells Fargo (WFC), Citigroup (C), Domino’s Pizza (DPZ), and Johnson & Johnson (JNJ), among others, reporting today. For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com Comments posted here will also appear on symbol pages. First Solar Inc. (FSLR) stock slipped overnight after Morningstar slashed its fair value estimate, warning that expiring U.S. solar tax credits and fierce competition could squeeze profits even as surging AI data center power demand creates a new growth opportunity. First Solar stock edged 0.7% lower overnight, ahead of Tuesday, after a 1% climb in the regular session. Morningstar analyst Bischof lowered his fair value estimate for the solar panel maker to $191 per share from $206, saying the stock was trading close to its estimated worth as of Monday. The firm maintained its no-economic-moat assessment and ‘Very High Uncertainty’ Rating for First Solar. The analyst believes intense competition and pressure on manufacturing costs prevent the company from building a lasting competitive advantage. The revised valuation reflects weaker expectations for solar panel sales after tax incentives begin expiring in the early 2030s. However, Bischof said First Solar could benefit from growing electricity needs associated with artificial intelligence, data centers and advanced manufacturing. Unlike most solar companies that use silicon, First Solar makes panels with a thin-film material called cadmium telluride. Its manufacturing process reduces dependence on Chinese suppliers, and its panels can perform better in hot and humid weather. The company is also the largest solar module manufacturer headquartered in the Western Hemisphere. Its strong position in the U.S. utility-scale market, where Morningstar estimates it has historically held about 30% market share, gives it an edge as domestic manufacturing policies favor local production. Still, the firm cautions that First Solar's manufacturing costs per watt remain somewhat higher than those of silicon-based competitors. The broader industry has become price-driven as manufacturing capacity expands and technological differences become less durable. First Solar’s pending orders fell to 45.1 gigawatts in June from 50.1 gigawatts at the end of 2025, as it delivered more panels than it secured in new deals. However, existing orders still give investors an idea of the company’s future sales. Morningstar expects First Solar to increase its production capacity to 22 gigawatts by the end of 2027, with investments in the U.S. and India. The firm also expects panel prices to rise slightly in the next few years before falling as tax benefits are reduced. The firm's valuation includes U.S. production credits worth $0.17 per watt. These incentives remain important to profit, making future policy decisions a major risk for investors. First Solar held approximately $1.7 billion in cash and investments at the end of June. Bischof views the company's conservative spending approach and early investment in U.S. manufacturing positively. However, Morningstar warns that the company's dependence on U.S. policy, concentrated sales markets, and an uncertain overseas manufacturing outlook could lead to widely varying financial results. While rising power demand could drive growth, the analyst believes the current share price already reflects First Solar's estimated value. (V) said on Tuesday it received approval from China’s central bank to begin preparing to set up a domestic bankcard clearing institution. This brings the U.S. payments network a step closer to entering China’s domestic payments market. V shares were up more than 1% in the overnight session at the time of writing. Visa said the People’s Bank of China (PBOC) approved its application to begin formal preparations for domestic operations. A local clearing institution would let the company settle domestic yuan transactions directly through its own network. Ryan McInerney, Chief Executive Officer of Visa, described the approval as a “significant step forward” in the company’s commitment to China.He also acknowledged the role of U.S. and Chinese leaders in “pursuing a constructive and strategically stable relationship between the world’s largest economies.” Visa first applied to establish a bankcard clearing institution in China in May 2020. Since then, the company has worked with Chinese banks on dual-branded cards, with China’s UnionPay handling domestic transactions and Visa processing overseas payments. In January, Visa said cards issued in mainland China could be linked to Apple Pay for overseas use. The approval follows diplomatic engagement between President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping. Trump raised Visa’s request for access to China’s domestic market during his Beijing visit in May. In September, China’s Ministry of Commerce said it would review and approve applications from foreign financial institutions, including U.S.-funded firms, seeking to operate or set up branches in the country. McInerney joined Trump’s business delegation to Beijing in May and became chair of the US-China Business Council in June. Visa’s rivals have already made progress in China’s domestic payments market. Mastercard’s (MA) Chinese joint venture began processing payments in 2024 after receiving approval in February 2020 to prepare for bankcard clearing operations. American Express (AXP) was the first of the three to receive a processing license in June 2020, after the PBOC approved it in 2018. Shares of Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX) slipped 0.6% overnight heading into Tuesday as Raymond James called fears of a near-term Starlink challenge to T-Mobile “overblown,” while Morningstar said Verizon’s network gives established carriers a significant edge. SPCX stock closed Monday at $163.42, up 0.5%, after gaining 2% last week for a second straight weekly gain. “We believe the recent fears over competition from SpaceX are overblown, as they are 3+ years away from becoming reality, and competition from larger players is nothing new to T-Mobile,” Raymond James said. The firm raised its rating on T-Mobile to 'Outperform' from 'Market Perform' and set a $170 price target, implying a 12% upside from current levels. SpaceX agreed last week to acquire Grain Management’s nationwide 800-megahertz spectrum portfolio, which includes up to 14 megahertz of paired spectrum. Grain had acquired the licenses from T-Mobile earlier in 2026. The transaction has been reported at around $8 billion. Meanwhile, Morningstar said SpaceX’s spectrum deal raises uncertainty for wireless carriers, but its base case remains that Starlink will not threaten their wireless operations. It raised its uncertainty ratings for Verizon, T-Mobile and AT&T to 'High' from 'Medium' and said SpaceX still needs more spectrum and thousands of sites to build a competitive ground network. Morningstar noted that Verizon has the weakest low-band spectrum position among the three major carriers, but still holds more than three times the low-band spectrum depth in most areas. Building a large terrestrial network could be a poor use of capital in a mature market, the firm said, although SpaceX has deep pockets. In a LinkedIn post from last week, T-Mobile’s CTO said, “You can acquire spectrum in a single transaction. You cannot acquire a nationwide, high-performing wireless network overnight.” He put Starlink Mobile’s holdings at 80 megahertz after the proposed acquisition, some of it uplink-only, compared with T-Mobile’s nearly 400 megahertz of low-band and mid-band spectrum. Building that network, he said, takes years of investment and construction. Wireless networks are built “site by site, neighborhood by neighborhood,” he wrote, including coverage inside buildings and other hard-to-reach places. Stifel reaffirmed its 'Buy' rating and $190 price target on SpaceX, implying a 17% upside from current levels. The firm called the spectrum acquisition “a new investment in SPCX’s mobile business” and said it advances SpaceX’s wireless plans alongside approval for up to 15,000 next-generation Starlink Mobile satellites. Stifel outlined three possible paths for SpaceX: build a terrestrial network, partner with existing operators or develop a different architecture. Telecom analyst Roger Entner said SpaceX could build a "massive" midband spectrum position if it secured additional spectrum associated with Ligado and Viasat and won licenses in a proposed FCC auction. This brings AST SpaceMobile's spectrum strategy under fresh scrutiny. ASTS stock rose nearly 1% to $51.46 on Monday, recovering slightly after a 16% slide over the previous two sessions. The selloff followed SpaceX’s agreement last week to acquire Grain Management’s nationwide 800-megahertz spectrum portfolio, putting the satellite-to-phone spectrum race back in focus. Entner said major carriers are likely to contest the 25 megahertz of spectrum the FCC has proposed auctioning. “Every major carrier will likely bid on these licenses for either offensive or defensive reasons,” he said. His bigger scenario is based on Ligado and Viasat. “If Elon Musk acquires Ligado and Viasat and secures this new spectrum, Starlink could control a massive midband block for terrestrial and direct to device services,” Entner said. On the other hand, ARK Investment Management analyst Tasha Keeney sees SpaceX’s recent spectrum deal and satellite authorization as building blocks for a broader mobile push. “Together, the two moves give Starlink Mobile a credible path to becoming a full mobile carrier instead of a dead-zone backup,” she said. Keeney said low-band spectrum could improve indoor coverage, while ground radios and small cellular units linked to Starlink dish infrastructure could add capacity where needed. The FCC is seeking comment on auctioning spectrum in the 1675–1695 MHz and 2020-2025 MHz bands. Its proposal would allow flexible use for terrestrial wireless, direct-to-device service or both. Final rules and an auction date have not been set. The bands sit next to the spectrum associated with AWS-4, Ligado and Viasat. SpaceX already has a major satellite step in place: The FCC authorized it to deploy up to 15,000 next-generation satellites for direct-to-device service. SpaceX says the system will work with spectrum around 2 GHz and deliver substantially more bandwidth than its current generation. SpaceX has agreed to acquire Grain Management’s nationwide 800 MHz portfolio, including up to 14 MHz of paired low-band spectrum. The deal still needs FCC approval. Neither company disclosed the price, though reports have put it at $8 billion. The low-band frequencies can travel farther and penetrate buildings better than higher-frequency signals, helping address a weakness of satellite-to-phone service. SpaceX’s plans also call for ground-based radios on towers, rooftops and other structures. Keeney has pointed to small cellular units connected to Starlink dish infrastructure as another way to add capacity, while noting that dish locations may not line up with areas of high mobile demand. AST’s own spectrum plans hinge on a conditional arrangement with Ligado. Under a 2025 term sheet, AST would receive long-term rights to use up to 40 MHz of Ligado’s L-band spectrum in the U.S. and Canada, plus access to 5 MHz in the 1670-1675 MHz band. The segment borders the lower edge of the FCC’s proposed 1675–1695 MHz auction band. While AST SpaceMobile relies on carrier partnerships to connect its satellites with ordinary phones, SpaceX is assembling a more direct mobile-network model that combines satellites, spectrum and ground infrastructure. Navitas Semiconductor (NVTS) stock gained overnight after the company unveiled a 24-kilowatt (kW) power delivery board developed with Nvidia (NVDA) to improve AI data center efficiency. Navitas targets 97% efficiency with the system, reduced power losses, and greater space savings. Navitas Semiconductor stock traded over 1% higher overnight, ahead of Tuesday. The stock fell 7% to its worst day in over a month in the regular session. Developed with Nvidia, Navitas’ 24-kilowatt board eliminates an intermediate conversion stage that traditionally changes 50 volts to 12 volts. By removing this step, the system aims to cut energy losses, simplify power distribution, and free up space on circuit boards The product expands Navitas' portfolio of high-voltage power solutions for AI infrastructure. It follows a previously announced 20 kW system that converts 800 volts to 6 volts, also developed along with Nvidia. Navitas expects the new board to achieve 97% efficiency at full power, with power density exceeding 2,000 watts per cubic inch. Its design follows a 400-by-60-millimeter format developed for Nvidia's latest systems, allowing installation on the compute motherboard near the processors. Placing power conversion closer to graphics processing units and other compute processors can help limit electricity losses as power travels through a system. The board is designed to supply an entire compute tray, addressing the substantial energy requirements of advanced AI computing equipment. The system uses 16 gallium nitride (GaN) transistors at 650 volts. Navitas’ GaNFast technology and dual-cooling design help convert power efficiently while keeping the system compact. “The next era of AI will be defined not only by how much compute we can create, but by our ability to deliver the power needed to unleash its full potential,” said Chris Allexandre, President and CEO, Navitas. title: Run game paves way for Monmouth's dominant first-ever win over UNH - Asbury Park Press
content: It's one thing to break down a longstanding barrier, it's another bulldoze right through it. Monmouth football did the latter on Saturday afternoon in Durham, N.H. For four straight years, the Hawks had lost to New Hampshire since joining the Coastal Athletic Association in 2022. They made sure that the fifth opportunity would erase any lingering memories of those past disappointments. Monmouth went on the road and dominated the Wildcats for four quarters, getting their first-ever victory over New Hampshire in a 42-21 rout to improve to 5-2 and remain unbeaten in conference play. "On the road, winning a CAA game is huge," Monmouth head coach Jeff Gallo said. "It's about this team, this year, and our opportunity to come get this game and make a point. It's for our former players who played these games and lost some tough ones to them. And I felt good going into it. We fought all the way through. We started fast, we out-physicaled them, and we took control of the game." The final score would be enough of a testament to the team's dominant effort, but the manner in which the win unfolded further reflected the emphatic showing by the Hawks. FCS No. 20 Monmouth ran the ball 62 times for 326 yards and four touchdowns. Both Kenny Smith Jr. (175) and Elijah Jennings (126) surpassed the century mark on the day on what was easily the team's most prolific ground performance of the season. The Hawks raced out of the gates and never looked back. After forcing a three-and-out, Monmouth ran the ball with Jennings on the first six plays of the game before the seventh was a 2-yard touchdown run by former Keyport standout Nazir Treadwell, who added 22 more rushing yards to the impressive total. After another UNH three-and-out, the Hawks' second drive of the game was the start of a career day for Smith, as five of the seven plays were runs to the redshirt freshman including the 6-yard touchdown to finish it and give Monmouth a 14-0 lead midway through the first quarter. "We wanted to come up here and be the more physical team, the more energized team," Gallo said. "To be able to run the ball into the wind and find some throws with the wind at our back. And I think just the o-line and running backs, we set the tone." The Hawks were also the beneficiaries of several New Hampshire lapses that combined with difficult windy conditions to put the Wildcats in an early hole. There were several drops, offset by many overthrows, as the UNH offense couldn't get anything going in the first half. To further exasperate the situation for the home team, swirling winds undermined any attempts by either team to punt. That was less of an issue for Monmouth, who started in opposing territory on four of their first six drives and each of those resulted in a touchdown. Monmouth seized on New Hampshire's struggles and capitalized on every opportunity. The strong run game set up a play action pass from quarterback Frankie Weaver to Tra Neal for 35-yard touchdown to extend the lead to 21-0 after the first quarter. Weaver finished the day 16-for-25 for 195 yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions, while Neal had a team-high 82 receiving yards on five catches. After the offense stalled slightly on the two next possessions, the Hawks finished the half strong by going back to the run game. The wide-open running lanes were cleared by upperclassmen that had experienced the years of struggles against New Hampshire, like senior center Kevin Shriner, guard Michael Petito, and tight end Shane Garrett, all of whom got to enjoy the catharsis of a physically-dominating effort upfront. For Garrett, that effort was appropriately rewarded with a play action touchdown pass from Weaver to close out the first half with a 28-0 lead. It was the first career touchdown reception for the redshirt junior from Ocean Township. "He's a program kid. He works his butt off. He's everything you want in a player," Gallo "Shore kid, great family, son of a coach. He comes to work every day and he does all the dirty work. And when we throw it to him, he's gonna catch it." New Hampshire's offensive challenges were exacerbated by the Monmouth defense, and the Wildcats decided to make quarterback change after starter Brooks Bentley was just 3-for-11 for 29 yards at halftime. That did appear to slightly spark the Wildcats momentarily, as they opened the second half by forcing a three-and-out and then running back Myles Thomason, a former Seton Hall Prep standout, authored a two-play drive with 44 rushing yards and a touchdown. But that would be the only glimmer of hope for New Hampshire. The Hawks answered with a nine-play, 75-yard drive that culminated with a 27-yard touchdown by Smith. The Hawks carried a 35-7 lead until the final five minutes, when both teams added late points with the game already decided. Those seven points allowed until garbage time are strong testament to the Monmouth defense, which took advantage of the New Hampshire mistakes and created plenty of negative plays on their own. Ryan Russo had a crucial forced fumble that set up the Hawks' touchdown before halftime. Mounir Keshen and JJ Lewis both contributed sacks, an impressive showing for two front four players that are also reliable run defenders. And a third down pressure by Jahide Lesaine resulted in an interception by Jaeden Jones in the third quarter. The win is quite the milestone for the Hawks. It's obviously always a breakthrough to get a first-ever win against a conference opponent, but it was also encouraging that there was no lag in the team's performance coming out of the bye week. Furthermore, it was their first game since Monmouth rejoined the FCS top 25 two weeks ago. They'll likely see another rankings bump after the decisive victory. More importantly, the Hawks continue to sit atop the CAA standings as the only 4-0 team in conference play. Monmouth got a big boost from Albany on Saturday, as the Great Danes knocked off rival Stony Brook 48-31. The Seawolves were the only other remaining unbeaten in the CAA that Monmouth doesn't play this season, and their loss means the Hawks control their own destiny to a conference title. No. 18 Campbell (6-1, 3-0) and Bryant (5-2, 3-0) are the other remaining unbeaten teams in league play. Monmouth will be on the road next Saturday against 1-6 Hampton and will need to not look past that game even as a Halloween showdown at home against Bryant looms. "Focus on what matters, and that's playing your best football," Gallo said. "Was it our best football? No. We can play better. We played relatively well, but there's room for improvement. And now we focus on the next one at Hampton and we're gonna bring the same mentality. It's a road game in the CAA. It's their homecoming. It's a great opportunity for us and a great challenge. The rankings don't matter to me, it's more about how we play." Obviously a recurring theme for the Hawks is one-week seasons and that will need to continue to avoid any let downs before the key matchup against Bryant in two weeks. But for this week's season, finally beating New Hampshire carried a bit more weight and thusly, a bit more cathartic relief. "We were aware that we hadn't beaten them, but it was about this team, this year, this game," Gallo said. "We came out and really got after it, which was great to see. And it's great for our alumni, it's great for our university, it's great for our fans. It's a good program win." With the wild winds limiting the options in the passing game to create offensive balance, the Hawks became more dynamic in the run game with a wide variety of designs and formations to keep the New Hampshire defense off-balance. The periphery movement and unique formations were clever disguises for a rushing attack that also deployed several counter punches in addition to straightforward dominance at the line of scrimmage. The first two touchdowns epitomized what worked so well for the Monmouth offense on Saturday. On the first score, Nazir Treadwell came out in a variation of the usual goal line wildcat formation, which was tweaked to sub out the quarterback for an extra blocker. Tra Neal motioned in for a chip on the left side, creating enough space for G/H power (guard and h-back pulling) to clear the way to the end zone. The second score was a more conventional variation of a similar concept. This time the Hawks came out in a pistol unbalanced formation and motioned Gavin Nelson to be the chip blocker and again they pulled the left guard Collin Goetter on power. But instead of a second puller, the "H" element was in insert block from tight end Marcus Middleton, paving the way for Kenny Smith on the 6-yard touchdown. In the second quarter, the Hawks used an even bolder design to spark an explosive run play. Monmouth initially came out in an ace set with two slot receivers to the left, motioned tight end to the right for a twins set, and then pulled center Kevin Shriner and guard Reed Collins on a what appeared to be a buck sweep to the short side of the field. The look allowed Smith to turn the corner for a 33-yard gain. The play actions looks were more conventional, although the last touchdown of the first half to Shane Garrett was interesting. Garrett lined up in the slot and then motioned across to give the appearance of split zone, but he raced to the flat in what appeared to be a lower red zone run-pass option for Frankie Weaver as opposed to straight play action. And the third layer to the various designs helped put the game out of reach. The Hawks got their first touchdown of the second half on a really fascinating run design. The Hawks came out with trips to the left and Smith also aligned to the left of Weaver, a de facto quads set to the short side of the field. The lone receiver to the right, Keshawn Mister, moved backwards across the formation to give a reverse look, which cleared the space for the play's true intent: a G/H sweep with Goetter and Middleton pulling to clear the way for Smith's 27-yard touchdown. What is very cool about that play is that it is a Wing-T concept in principle with the misdirection, but executed out of a traditional spread formation. With an additional bye week to prepare and the motivation to beat New Hampshire for the first time, the Hawks brought out some of their best run designs in the win. There were some intriguing defensive fronts, particularly on third down, that the Monmouth defense used to stifle a New Hampshire offense that also shot itself in the foot. But instead of focusing on the X's and the O's, it's time to highlight some Jimmys and Joes that are emerging for the Hawks. JJ Lewis has to be at the top of the list. The senior joined Monmouth last year as a transfer from D-II Findlay, and he has come into his own this fall. In addition to his sack, he recovered Russo's first fumble that led to the key score before halftime. He is second on the team with three sacks and also has two pass break ups. His ability to be a disruptive presence on the interior is a huge boost for the front four as a whole, as the interior is usually shaped by stalwart run defenders. Lewis has shown the ability to do both. Complimenting him on the edge is Mounir Keshen, who continues his ascent as a premier defender, and Hunter Watson. So much of Monmouth's sack production last year was on third down in clear passing situations, but Watson and Keshen have emerged as premier rushers on early downs in addition to being stout against the run. Keshen leads the team with 3.5 sacks while Watson also has three. The growth of the trio of Watson, Keshen and Lewis has the potential to be a game-changer for the Hawks down the stretch. With limited angles on the broadcast of a road game, it's challenging to assess exactly what's happening in the secondary. The Hawks continue to use a deep rotation of players with varying results, as positive flashes can also be offset by maddening lapses. But the bright spot continues to be the safeties. Jaeden Jones is of course a star, but Donovan Fey had several excellent moments against UNH. He seemed to recognize a potential coverage breakdown in pre-snap, and recovered to the seam for a key pass breakup in the first half. He can be a nightmare for opposing receivers, delivering punishing hits while attacking the catch point to separate his man from the ball. Aside from some late coverage lapses and two runs by Myles Thomason that went for 44 yards and a score, this was a lights-out performance from the Monmouth defense. The Hawks will look to build on it next week against Hampton. We may earn a commission when you buy through links on this page. title: College football: No. 23 Monmouth rides ground game past UNH, 42-21 - Seacoastonline.com
content: DURHAM — The University of New Hampshire football team dropped a 42-21 decision to No. 23 Monmouth on Saturday, Oct. 17 at Wildcat Stadium. Monmouth rushed for 301 yards and scored six touchdowns to improve to 5-2 overall and 4-0 in conference play. New Hampshire dropped to 2-6 overall and 1-4 in the CAA. Sophomore linebacker Trevor Barry led the Wildcats defensively with a career-high 20 tackles, including 12 solo stops. Grad student safety Jackson Stone added a career-best 16 tackles and surpassed the 100-career tackle mark, while sophomore safety Cohen Cook made 12 tackles. Sophomore linebacker Matthew Sopp also registered a personal-best 10 tackles. Monmouth's rushing attack controlled the game, led by Kenny Smith Jr., who ran 27 times for 175 yards and two touchdowns. Elijah Jennings added 126 yards and a touchdown on 28 carries. Quarterback Frankie Weaver completed 16 of 25 passes for 195 yards and two touchdowns. The Wildcats received offensive contributions from several players. Grad student running back Myles Thomason rushed for 70 yards on seven carries, and scored on an 11-yard touchdown run. Junior wide receiver Ty Carlson led New Hampshire's receiving corps with 62 yards, including a 41-yard touchdown reception. Sophomore quarterback Tommy McLeish entered in the second half and sparked the offense, completing 13 of 19 passes for 178 yards while directing three touchdown drives. The Wildcats return to action Oct. 24 when they travel to Merrimack. New Hampshire's next home game is Nov. 7 against Rhode Island. We may earn a commission when you buy through links on this page. title: David Ismail ends scoring drought, leads Vermont soccer to comeback win over UNH - Yahoo Sports
content: David Ismail ended a two-month scoring drought and Vermont soccer prolonged a yearslong home unbeaten streak typical Catamount fashion: A second-half comeback with a late-regulation winner. Ismail, who scored for the first time since Aug. 23 with a first-half penalty strike, blasted in the go-ahead goal in the 84th minute, capping Vermont's rally for a 3-2 victory over New Hampshire in front of 2,197 at windy Virtue Field on Saturday, Oct. 17. No. 16 Vermont (9-1-3, 3-0-1), which trailed 2-1 at the break, also extended its regular-season home unbeaten run to 27 consecutive games (19-0-8), a streak that started on Oct. 27, 2023. "Love the guys' response. What a great second-half attitude and what a way to turn the tide … and never give up," said Vermont first-year head coach Adrian Dubois, who is an UNH alum. "That is what Vermont football is. When you do that, good things are going to happen." DAVID ISMAIL WITH THE BRACE IN THE 84TH MINUTE 🚨🚨Vermont takes a 3-2 lead! Halim Bangura and Luis Vetter each tally an assist on UVM's third goal 😼#LetsRally pic.twitter.com/q4nCl1fPUD After Vermont was rewarded a PK following an officials' video review, Ismail converted from the spot in the 10th minute for a 1-0 lead. But the Catamounts, challenged by the windy conditions on defense, conceded a pair of goals in the 24th and 32nd minute, respectively. On the first UNH goal, Laurin Preuss supplied a pretty flick via Ryo Myata's corner kick that slipped under the bar to level the game. Then David Dravila rolled a shot past Vermont goalie Niklas Herceg (four saves), a goal that was initially ruled offside before another review overturned the call. In the second half, Ismail had two door-step chances with headers — the first smacked off the cross bar, the second UNH goalie Aaron Choi (five saves) snatched above his head. But in the 70th minute, the Catamounts found the equalizer via Philipp Schmidtke's fifth goal of 2026. A failed UNH clearance in the box fell to Schmidtke, who uncorked a lefty blast inside the left post. On the winner, Ismail uncorked a lefty rocket into the back of the net with authority for the 84th-minute winner, also his fifth goal this fall. "He's a top player. He's going to find a way. I'm just happy for him because he's the hardest worker on the team," Dubois said of Ismail. "That's going to give him a boost of energy and we need our best guys playing well right now. He had a really good game overall." Vermont travels to Albany for its next game on Saturday, Oct. 24. Contact Alex Abrami at aabrami@freepressmedia.com. title: UNH Stock Rises Overnight Ahead Of Earnings: Analyst Outlines ‘Short Premium’ Play To Cut January Call Cost By Nearly 60% - Stocktwits
content: UnitedHealth (UNH) is set to report third-quarter (Q3) earnings before Tuesday’s market open, with options pricing in a 6.5% move around the results. Tidal Financial Group strategist Michael Khouw says elevated options prices create an opportunity for traders to sell November premium to help finance a cheaper January call. UNH stock rose 0.9% in after-hours trading on Monday after closing the regular session down 0.2% at $378.52. “The only thing more expensive than health insurance is perhaps the costs of insuring shares of health insurers,” Khouw said, pointing to UnitedHealth as an example. Options imply a 6.5% move in UnitedHealth shares around earnings, while implied volatility is running at about 40%, about twice the stock’s realized volatility of 20%, he said. The implied move is the second-largest in almost two years. Shares have fallen after five of their past eight earnings reports, including nearly 20% drops after results in January and April 2025, CNBC noted. Khouw’s proposed trade is a “short premium” strategy: It sells two November options to collect $10.60 per share and offset part of the cost of a longer-dated call. The trade buys a January 2027 $400 call for $18.20 per share, then sells a November $420 call for $5.80 and a November $340 put for $4.80. The resulting net cost is $7.60 per share, or $760 per contract, reducing the call’s upfront cost by about 58%. If UnitedHealth finishes November between $340 and $420: The short options would expire worthless. The January call’s breakeven would be $407.60 at expiration. If UNH stock falls below $340: The short put could require the seller to buy shares at that price, for an effective cost of about $347.60 per share after the trade’s net debit. Khouw said UnitedHealth had been essentially flat over five years and traded 12% to 13% below the midpoint of its two-year high-low range. At about 17 times forward earnings, he said, the stock was not priced for a recovery. He sees the company’s 13% to 16% earnings-growth target as achievable, though rising healthcare costs is a headwind. Khouw also pointed to enrollment trends. Affordable Care Act (ACA) marketplace enrollment appears poised to decline, he said, although the segment is smaller than Medicare and commercial coverage. Commercial fee-based enrollment grew about 2.9% from 2024 to 2025, while total Medicare enrollment rose 4.5%. Commercial growth exceeded U.S. workforce growth of about 1.4%. Koyfin’s estimates for the upcoming quarter compare with the last reported quarter. They show revenue of $111.49 billion, down 0.5% sequentially. Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) is estimated at $6.47 billion, down 28%, while earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT) is forecast at $5.44 billion, down 32%. GAAP earnings per share (EPS) are projected to fall 36.81%. Fiscal.ai’s year-over-year estimates show revenue of $112.4 billion, compared with $113.2 billion a year earlier. It forecasts EBITDA of $6.45 billion, up from $5.25 billion, and earnings per share of $3.06, compared with $2.92. TD Cowen lowered its price target on UNH to $402 from $430, implying a 6% upside, while maintaining a 'Buy' rating. The firm expects preliminary commentary on 2027 earnings-per-share expectations with the report. Meanwhile, Piper Sandler said 66.8% of UnitedHealth members were enrolled in plans rated four stars or higher, based on September 2026 enrollment data, and called the company’s resilience “impressive” and underappreciated. Oppenheimer noted that the share of members in four-star-or-higher plans fell 15% at UnitedHealth for 2027, versus 10% at Elevance Health, 15% at CVS Health and 9% at Centene. Humana moved in the opposite direction, with 95% of its members in four-star-or-higher plans, up from 42% a year earlier. His warning came after a mixed Monday session: the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY) slipped 0.06%, the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) fell 0.7%, and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) gained 0.35%, while the S&P 500 hovered near its record high set the previous week. “The market is not so conducive right now,” Burry said in a Substack chat. “Lots of these stocks, you have to respect the new highs. Might be a bull trap, and a number of big bear markets have started that way.” His challenge, he said, is staying positioned until his view plays out: “I just know where this will be in a few years. The trick is to get there.” Burry added that Puts account for about 10% of his portfolio. Long positions and LEAPS make up most of the rest, with minimal cash. “If the market crashes hard, I think I’ll do ok,” he said, adding that he expects his long holdings to perform over three to five years. “A year is nothing.” Burry’s reluctance to add shorts does not mean he has dropped his bearish bets. In his most recent Substack post, he said almost all his short exposure was expressed through puts on the Nasdaq-100 and semiconductor stocks. The options expire in 2027 and were 20% out of the money. He put his window for a significant market top at zero to nine months. Burry sold his Fannie and Freddie common shares and added them to junior preferred stock (JPS). When asked how he moved from Fannie common into Freddie common and then out of both, he replied: “Almost as soon as I dumped the Fannie into Freddie, I was not comfortable with my risk position and started moving all and then some into the JPS.” The preferred shares rank above common stock in the capital structure. Burry’s thesis is that they could benefit if the government resolves its senior claims and reinstates preferred dividends. He said the junior preferreds could trade well above par depending on interest rates, adding that the potential return “from current levels” could reach four to five times. The main risk is the Treasury’s senior preferred stock liquidation preference, which Burry puts at about $388 billion, about twice the companies’ combined book value. If the claims were converted into common shares, existing common shareholders could face severe dilution. Burry sees the junior preferreds as better positioned in that scenario. He is optimistic that a resolution favorable to both common and preferred shareholders could come within two years. But he said on chat that the delay had made him “antsy,” citing a “quickly deteriorating” multifamily housing situation. Meanwhile, Burry sees the Trump administration as a key factor. He doubts that a lengthy IPO process fits the president’s appetite: “He wants big wins,” Burry said. “He clearly is bored easily and does not tolerate too many details shoved in his face.” He called Trump “almost incompatible” with the IPO process. But Burry argued that resolving the senior preferred stock and its liquidation preference does not depend on an IPO. “The easiest thing in the world to do would be to cancel the SPS and the Liquidation Preference,” he said. “And they have not done it. That says something.” Government warrants expire before the 2028 election, Burry said, which could force action, though they could also be extended. “Treasury/FHFA holds all the cards here,” he said, adding that some action is needed before the end of Trump’s term. When asked about Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, Burry replied: “He’s toeing a line a lot more than I thought he would.” Both FNMA and FMCC have fallen for seven straight weeks and are on track for their worst annual run since 2010. Recently, Mizuho downgraded both stocks and cut their price targets. The firm estimated the odds of fast privatization by 2028 at 18% for Fannie and 9% for Freddie. Economist Peter Schiff was more bearish, calling a Fannie-Freddie IPO “always a pipe dream” and its rally as “just a pump-and-dump scheme.” He noted that the stocks were down nearly 80% from their September 2025 highs. Micron fell 4% on Monday, while other memory and storage companies, including SK Hynix, Samsung, SanDisk, Seagate and Western Digital, also declined after Chinese chipmaker ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) outlined plans for a new DDR5 server-memory product. CXMT said it aims to launch a server memory module using a “4F square” DRAM design by the end of the year. The architecture aims to pack more memory cells into the same chip area as the 6F square design widely used today, potentially increasing density. Musk contrasted China’s manufacturing scale on X with SpaceX’s launch lead. “When China figures out how to manufacture a product, their ability to scale is often greater than the rest of the world combined,” he said, citing lithium batteries and solar. He said SpaceX is a “rare counter-example”: it puts an order of magnitude more mass into orbit than the rest of the world, although China now accounts for most non-SpaceX mass to orbit. “SpaceX is an anomaly in the matrix,” he added. Musk then turned to memory chips, noting that RAM was a “low margin commodity” only about three years ago. He said LPDDR5 and LPDDR6 share a common standard that China “seems to be solving fast,” while newer high-bandwidth memory architectures, an SRAM layer beneath logic, 3D-stacked RAM above logic and the challenge of cooling the logic will be “harder to solve.” Musk’s comments follow SpaceX’s August earnings call, when he said memory supply was struggling to keep pace with AI-driven demand. He said memory output was growing about 20% a year while demand was increasing 200% or more, a gap he said could push prices higher. The supply issue matters to SpaceX’s expansion into AI computing, alongside its launch and Starlink businesses. Under a multi-year Google cloud-services agreement disclosed in June, Google is set to pay SpaceX $920 million a month from October 2026 through June 2029 for access to computing capacity, including about 110,000 Nvidia GPUs and related infrastructure with memory. The company reported $15.8 billion in AI-related capital expenditures, within about $18.4 billion in total capital expenditures. Revenue reached $7.8 billion, while SpaceX recorded a $541 million net loss. Musk is also pursuing a longer-term chip-supply strategy through Terafab, a Texas facility to make, package and test logic and memory chips. Intel joined the project in April, with its 14A manufacturing process expected to be used at the fab. In August, SpaceX and Tesla announced an initial $16.8 billion investment in the project. Musk also said recently that TSMC could potentially sublease part of the facility, while Tesla and SpaceX would retain ownership. title: Wrong-way crash on I-91 in North Haven leaves 1 dead, several injured - WFSB
content:
NORTH HAVEN, Conn. (WFSB) - A multi-vehicle crash caused by a wrong-way driver on I-91 southbound in North Haven left one person dead on Friday night. Troopers were called to the area of I-91 south near Exit 9 at around 11:43 p.m. after reports of a wrong-way driver where the vehicle was then involved in a multi-vehicle crash, according to state police. EMS and fire department personnel also responded to the scene, and the Connecticut Department of Transportation assisted with road closures. A man driving a Honda Accord was heading southbound on I-91 in the left lane while a man driving a pick up truck was traveling the wrong-way and struck his car in a head-on collision. The man who’s vehicle was struck then entered the left-center lane, where it was struck by another vehicle, a Jeep. The man then entered the right lane and right shoulder, where it was struck by a GMC SUV, state police said. State Police have identified the driver of the Honda Accord that was struck as 21-year-old Ryan O’Shea from Stony Point, New York. The University of New Haven confirmed that he was a criminal justice major with a concentration in police science at the school. He interned last summer with the New York City Police Department, where he hoped to start his career as a police officer after commencement. He was also a senior captain of the university’s club hockey team. O’Shea suffered fatal injuries in the crash and died on scene. The driver of the GMC SUV was transported to a nearby hospital with serious injuries. Also, the driver and the front passenger who were in the Jeep were suffered minor injuries and were transported to a local hospital as well as the driver of the GMC. The State Police Collision Analysis and Reconstruction Squad responded to the scene and is assisting with the investigation. State Police said this remains under active investigation. title: Kidder Lecture and LGBTQ+ Resource Fair - University of New Hampshire
content: This annual event highlights issues related to LGBTQIA+ identities and inclusion. The lecture brings prominent speakers, scholars, and advocates to campus to engage the community in meaningful conversations about sexual orientation, gender identity, and belonging. The event serves as an opportunity for the members of the UNH Community to learn, reflect, and deepen their understanding of diverse experiences. The Kidder Lecture is followed by the LGBTQ+ Resource Fair. It brings together various on-campus departments and community-based organizations to highlight resources for members of the LGBTQ+ Members of the UNH Community and allies. The Kidder Lecture is supported by the Kidder Fund, established by William “Bill” Kidder, a UNH alumnus and former associate dean of students. The fund supports educational initiatives, awards, and programming that promote awareness and inclusion for individuals of diverse sexual orientations and gender identities. As a signature campus event, the Kidder Lecture and LGBTQ+ Resource Fair reflects UNH’s ongoing commitment to fostering an inclusive and welcoming community for all. For questions and additional information, please contact Ramonda "Monda" Kindle at Ramonda.Kindle@unh.edu Register Today for the 2026 Kidder Lecture and LGBTQ+ Resource Fair! Click Here for the 2026 Kidder Lecture Registration Form Please fill out the Registration Form no later than 11:59pm on October 19, 2026 in order to attend the event in-person. Virtual registrants will be accepted until Thursday, October 22, 2026 We are excited to announce Queerlective Founder and Executive Director Randall Nielsen as the keynote speaker for the 2026 Kidder Lecture. Date: Monday, October 26, 2026Time: 12:00 pm - 1:30 pm Location: Strafford Room, Memorial Union Building (MUB), Durham Campus The Resource Fair will immediately follow the Kidder Lecture from 1:30 pm - 5:00 pm. Lunch will be served for in-person Kidder Lecture guests Registration is on a first-come, first-served basis until the event is at capacity This event is open to all UNH undergraduate, graduate, and professional students, faculty, staff, administrators, and alumni 2026-2027 Chair: Ramonda Kindle, Aulbani J. Beauregard Center for Equity, Justice, and Freedom Christina Juris, Undergraduate Student Senate DEI Council Chair Sam Crawford, Graduate Student Senate Representative Kelsey Boucher, Clinical Associate Professor, School of Social Work Deborah Briand, Academic Department Coordinator, College of Liberal Arts Michelle Bronner, Deputy Director and Senior Woman Administrator, Athletics Lu Butterfield-Ferrell, Program Manager, New Hampshire Listens Holly Cashman, Professor, Department of Languages, Literature, and Culture Evan England, Assistant Director, Center for Social Policy in Practice Amanda Harvey, Administrative Coordinator, UNH Office for Faculty Excellence Sarah Leonard, Director of Child Study and Development Center, Human Development and Family Studies Elena Long, Associate Professor, College of Engineering and Physical Sciences Ally Twitchell, Coordinator for Student Involvement and Student Success, Manchester Campus Kai Uchida, Assistant Professor/University Archivist, Dimond Library Erica Vazza, Assistant Director of Engagement and Prevention, The SHARPP Center Linds Jakows discussed the importance of taking action for LGBTQIA+ Thriving: In and Outside of the Political System. UNH Alumnae Brady Barre discussed New Hampshire Outright and the importance of mutual aid. Tona Brown discussed her book, Tonacity: The Tona Brown Story. The event included an interview conducted by a UNH student, a Q&A, and a book signing opportunity. Sarah Leonard, UNH Early Childhood Teacher, UNH Child Study & Development Center Joelle Ryan, UNH Faculty, UNH Department of Women’s & Gender Studies Noele Lee, Lecturer, Decision Sciences, Paul College Laquincy (Lionel) Loveless, Officially Knotted Bowties, Portsmouth Frederic Mason, Executive Director, Large Cap Sector Specialist, J.P. Morgan Asset Management Trans UNH and UNH Stonewall Grads hosted a virtual film screening of Coded Black with a group discussion of the film.  Participants we encouraged to bring their dinner to the screening and shared their thoughts on the themes raised in the film and considered their responsibilities to addressing the issues highlighted. Simmons College Professor Gary Bailey explored the climate of amplification of homophobia, sexism, racism, and other biases. Participants examined the way we assign “outcast” status to people/groups within our communities and ways some people may unintentionally participate in the process even though they reject the beliefs. Robyn Ochs discussed building acceptance and respect for individual choice and political & legal legitimization for people’s gender, sexual and romantic identities.  The discussion concluded with advocating for the rights of people to live safely, openly and with full access and opportunity. Mara Keisling discussed the significance of advocating for the “T” in our LGBTQIA+ community at UNH and beyond and how to create a community where transphobia and microaggressions are eliminated. Erin E. Buzuvis discussed policies that the NCAA and various sport organizations adopted for the purpose of determining the eligibility of transgender athletics to compete according to their gender identities and advocated for policies that are as inclusive as possible under the circumstances particular to those organizations. The College of Liberal Arts hosted Roma Baran, and Anne Philbin to discuss their experiences at UNH and what each took away from their experiences that helped define where they are today. In an evening chat, Dr. Darrow shared his lived experiences as the former Chief of Behavioral and Prevention Research Branch, Division of STD/HIV Prevention at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and a consultant for World Health Organization, the European Union, and the Global Program on AIDS. title: UNH, HUM, CNC Stocks Rally On Medicare Advantage Rate Surprise - Stocktwits
content: Shares of insurers UnitedHealth Group (UNH), Centene (CNC), Humana (HUM), and Elevance Health (ELV) jumped in Monday’s extended trading hours after the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services announced that the payments to private insurers offering Medicare Advantage plans will increase 2.48% next year. This increase implies $13 billion in additional payments to Medicare insurers for the year, the agency said. “When accounting for estimated risk score trend in MA due to factors such as population changes and coding practices, this amounts to a 4.98% increase,” the agency added. The move came as a surprise since in January, the CMS had proposed a roughly flat increase in payments for private Medicare plans the following year, sending shares of insurers down and wiping out about $100 billion in stock market value. The announcement further comes as a relief to the industry plagued by concerns over rising medical costs. Shares of UNH, CNC, HUM and ELV rallied between 5% and 11% at the time of writing. Shares of Aetna parent CVS Health (CVS) rose by about 6.5% while Molina Healthcare (MOH) stock rose a modest 3%. While UnitedHealth is the largest provider of private Medicare Advantage plans in the U.S., Humana is the second largest. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around UNH stock rose from ‘bullish’ to ‘extremely bullish’ territory over the past 24 hours, while message volume increased from ‘normal’ to ‘high’ levels. Sentiment around HUM stock, meanwhile, increased from ‘neutral’ to ‘extremely bullish’ territory over the past 24 hours, while message volume rose from ‘normal’ to ‘extremely high’ levels. content: Shares of UnitedHealth Group, Inc. (UNH) are headed for their fourth monthly win as Wall Street turns more bullish after a large second-quarter (Q2) earnings beat and a sweeping increase to its 2026 outlook. UNH stock rose 1% on Friday, bringing its monthly gain to nearly 3%, while shares also finished the week marginally higher. BofA called UnitedHealth’s quarter “impressive,” noting that earnings beat consensus by 31% and guidance rose 12%. The firm raised its price target to $512, implying over 20% upside, while reiterating a ‘Buy’ rating and citing a “strong” quarter and broad-based outlook increase. Morgan Stanley was even more bullish, lifting its target to $529, implying a 24% upside. The firm said the Q2 beat and higher 2026 targets “validate its disciplined strategy and establish a stronger base for future growth.” Truist, Oppenheimer and KeyBanc each moved to $500 targets, implying a 17% upside. Truist highlighted top- and bottom-line beats, a better Medical Care Ratio, and improving expectations for UnitedHealthcare and Optum Health. Oppenheimer said that the company “handily” topped expectations, while KeyBanc said results “topped bullish expectations” and argued UnitedHealth could hit $30 in earnings per share (EPS) sooner than anticipated. Goldman Sachs and UBS both raised their targets to $490, implying a 15% upside. Goldman cited a “material” earnings beat, stronger Optum Health profitability and a larger-than-expected guidance increase. UBS said UnitedHealth was “making good progress with more to go.” Meanwhile, RBC Capital raised its target to $478, implying a 12% upside. It remained positive on the earnings beat and guidance hike but flagged investor concern around persistent commercial medical-cost pressure. UnitedHealth posted adjusted EPS of $6.38, beating the $4.92 consensus and rising from $4.08 a year ago. Revenue of $112.03 billion also topped estimates, while the medical care ratio improved to 86.7% from 89.4%. Additionally, the company raised its 2026 adjusted EPS outlook to $19.50-$20 from more than $18.25, lifted UnitedHealthcare’s operating profit forecast to at least $12 billion, and increased Optum Health’s outlook to at least $2.2 billion. CEO Stephen Hemsley said UnitedHealth was “returning to form” as stronger performance disciplines took hold. He reaffirmed the company’s 13%-16% long-term earnings-growth target and doubled the 2026 buyback goal to at least $5 billion. Medicare Advantage drove the beat, with costs coming in below expectations. “Medicare delivered a strong second quarter,” UnitedHealthcare CEO Tim Noel said. Commercial plans remained the weak spot, with medical-cost trends above 11%. On the other hand, Optum said its tools added nearly 200,000 patient-facing hours, cut clinician cognitive burnout by 90%, and achieved a 96% first-pass approval rate for digital prior authorizations. SPCX stock fell 5% on Friday, extending its weekly decline to 15%. “This is fake news,” Musk said on X in response to a post summarizing the reported agreement. Taiwan’s Economic Daily said that Hon Hai Precision Industry, better known as Foxconn, had secured its first contract to manufacture AI servers for SpaceX. According to the report, SpaceX was preparing to deploy more than 13,000 server racks built around Nvidia’s GB300 platform. The estimated $52 billion value was based on an assumed cost of $4 million per rack rather than a disclosed contract price. Citrini analyst Jukan said on X that Foxconn had displaced the dominance of Dell Technologies and Super Micro Computer in supplying AI server infrastructure to SpaceX. It also claimed deliveries would begin in late 2026 and continue into the first quarter of 2027. Chairman Young Liu has previously said Foxconn expects to capture more than 40% of the global AI server market, while shipments of advanced AI racks are projected to increase through the end of the year. A separate Wall Street Journal report on Friday said that SpaceX was in discussions with the U.S. Department of Defense about supplying data-center capacity worth several billion dollars for military AI workloads. The talks were said to be ongoing and could still fail to produce an agreement. SpaceX has also explored offering computing power to outside AI customers as it seeks to compete more directly with cloud infrastructure providers such as CoreWeave. In June, SpaceX also reached computing arrangements with Google and Anthropic. The Google deal covered access to about 110,000 Nvidia chips, while Anthropic secured capacity at the company’s Colossus 1 data center in Memphis. The potential Defense Department arrangement would deepen SpaceX’s already extensive relationship with the U.S. military. The Pentagon relies on the company for rocket launches, satellite communications and missile-tracking systems. It is also seeking more computing capacity as intelligence agencies and military units increase their use of AI. SpaceX employees have reportedly discussed selling computing capacity at prices designed to compete with established cloud and specialized AI infrastructure providers. The Pentagon, meanwhile, is seeking funding for a new AI Arsenal initiative centered on access to high-end chips and computing resources. She called Angermayer’s work with ATAI “one of the biggest catalysts of the psychedelic renaissance,” adding that clinical trials are increasingly validating the potential of psychedelics in treatment-resistant depression, post-traumatic stress disorder and broader mental health conditions. Wood also credited Angermayer with backing the field long before psychedelic medicine became widely accepted, fashionable, or investable. “Long before psychedelics were accepted, fashionable, or investable, Christian’s life’s mission was to reactivate them and bring back hope and health for those who had lost both,” she said. The deal marked a 26% premium to AtaiBeckley’s shareholders. The companies are targeting completion of the acquisition in the third quarter of 2026. The centerpiece of the deal is BPL-003, an intranasal psychedelic therapy being tested in late-stage studies for treatment-resistant depression. title: UnitedHealth's Q3 Margins Improve, But Membership Falls: Time to Buy? - TradingView
content: UnitedHealth Group Incorporated UNH showed further signs of a turnaround in the third quarter of 2026, with stronger earnings and improving profitability.Earnings beat expectations, medical costs eased, and management raised its annual outlook again. UNH shares jumped 7.4% since then. However, declining membership raises questions about whether the company can sustain its earnings recovery over the long term. UNH reported third-quarter adjusted earnings of $4.69 per share,beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $4.12 and rising 60.6% year over year.Revenues reached $112.7 billion, exceeding the consensus estimate by 1.2% but slipping from $113.2 billion last year. Operating earnings climbed to $6.6 billion from $4.3 billion, while net margin improved to 3.6% from 2.1%. The standout number was the medical care ratio, which measures the share of premium revenue spent on medical services. It fell to 88.4% from 89.9% a year ago. Even a modest improvement in this measure can have a large effect on earnings for an insurer of UnitedHealth's size. Lower claims pressure, tighter pricing and redesigned benefits helped drive the change. However, the quarter included $610 million of favorable medical reserve development related to 2026 care. Still, the operating cost ratio also improved to 12.8% from 13.5%, pointing to progress beyond claims alone. It again raised its 2026 adjusted earnings forecast to at least $20.50 per share from its previous $19.50-$20 range. For further details, see UNH Tops Q3 Earnings on Lower Medical Costs, Raises '26 Outlook. Are Better Margins Coming at the Expense of Growth? That is the central debate after earnings. UnitedHealthcare served 48.3 million people, down from 50.1 million a year ago. Medicare Advantage membership has fallen by 935,000 since the end of 2025 as the company withdrew from less attractive business and adjusted benefits. The financial payoff: UnitedHealthcare's operating profit increased to $2.8 billion from $1.8 billion despite lower revenue. Its operating margin climbed to 3.3% from 2.1%. Management now expects Medicare Advantage margins near the upper end of its 2-4% target range for 2026. Executives emphasized dual-eligible and chronic-condition plans alongside higher-value HMOs, rather than chasing enrollment across every product. More than 94% of Medicare-eligible Americans will have access to a UnitedHealthcare Medicare offering next year. A smaller, better-priced book seems healthier than growth that destroys profit. Still, a lasting turnaround requires enrollment to stabilize. Formal 2027 membership guidance remains ahead, making the upcoming selling season an important checkpoint. Optum offers another reason for optimism. Segment operating earnings rose to $3.7 billion from $2.5 billion even as revenue declined to $66.9 billion from $69.2 billion. Its margin expanded to 5.6% from 3.6%. Optum Health's turnaround was particularly notable. Operating earnings jumped to $735 million from just $41 million last year, with the margin reaching 3.2%. Revenue fell 10% as the business reduced exposure to markets where its value-based care operations lacked scale. Management expects further improvement in Optum Health's profitability in 2027 as it works toward its 6-8% margin target for 2028. Optum Insight's automation tools and Optum Rx's pharmacy operations offer additional earnings opportunities, but the company still must convert those initiatives into consistent growth. Optum Rx also faces pressure from lower prescription volumes tied to UnitedHealthcare's shrinking membership. Adjusted prescriptions declined to 393 million from 414 million. External customers now account for more than half its covered lives, however, reducing dependence on the insurance business. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 EPS is now pegged at $20.39, indicating 24.7% year-over-year growth. The earnings estimate has seen eight upward revisions over the past week against no downward movement. The consensus estimate for revenues is pegged at $447.4 billion, implying only a marginal decline from a year ago. For 2027, EPS is now projected to grow to $22.99, marking a 12.8% improvement. It has also seen seven upward estimate revisions in the past week, against no cuts. Revenues are pegged at $460.01 billion, indicating 2.8% growth from a year ago. The company beat earnings estimates in each of the past four quarters, producing an average earnings surprise of 14%. UnitedHealth Group Incorporated price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | UnitedHealth Group Incorporated Quote Medical utilization remains the biggest uncertainty. Management said that commercial medical cost trends remain above 11%, although they have stabilized recently. Management expects core Medicaid margins to remain negative but better than negative 1% in 2026, with improvement anticipated in 2027. Medicare Advantage quality ratings add another challenge. For 2027, at least 69% of UnitedHealthcare's Medicare Advantage members are in plans rated four stars or higher, down from approximately 78% for 2026, per reports.Lower ratings can weigh on future bonus payments and product competitiveness. Nevertheless, UnitedHealth is targeting approximately 75% for 2028. Cash generation and debt also deserve attention. Operating cash flow totaled $5.1 billion in the quarter, or 1.2 times net income. Debt represented 41.7% of capital at September's end. The company aims to approach 40% by year-end while funding investments, dividends and repurchases. Looking at the year-to-date period, UNH stock has gained 23.2%, outperforming the S&P 500’s 12.9% rise, but trailing the industry’s 26% growth. Peers like Molina Healthcare, Inc. MOH and Centene Corporation CNC have increased 22.5% and 71.4%, respectively, during this time. Price Performance – UNH, MOH, CNC, Industry & S&P 500 UNH trades at 18.50X forward earnings, above the industry average of 16.08X but below its five-year median of 19.02X. In comparison, Molina and Centene are currently priced at 24.07X and 13.44X, respectively, both higher than their own five-year median multiples. Wall Street also sees room for further gains. Despite the stock’s recent rise, the average analyst price target of $476.52 suggests an upside of 17.2% from current levels. Individual targets range from $380 to $529, indicating that analysts remain divided over the pace and extent of UnitedHealth's recovery. UnitedHealth's stronger third-quarter earnings, improving margins and raised guidance suggest that its turnaround is moving in the right direction. Upward earnings estimate revisions add to the positive outlook. Although declining membership, elevated utilization and Medicare Advantage rating pressures remain concerns, management’s focus on profitable growth should help strengthen results over time. UNH's valuation remains below its historical median, while Optum's improving profitability provides another reason for optimism. AAPL stock closed up nearly 2% higher on Thursday as Apple Intelligence AI service registration in China, alongside Wall Street optimism over the company’s recent strength, bolstered prices. ATAI stock jumped more than 33% at close after Eli Lilly (LLY) confirmed that it is acquiring the clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company. Meanwhile, UNH stock gained more than 1% after its second-quarter (Q2) earnings blew past Wall Street estimates and it also raised its full-year profit outlook. Shares of the iPhone maker clocked an all-time high of $334.68 on Thursday amid a series of positive catalysts for the company. China's cyberspace regulator on Wednesday approved the registration of Apple Intelligence for use on iPhones in the country, clearing a key regulatory hurdle for the long-awaited launch of Apple's AI features in the country. Under Chinese rules, companies must obtain approval for large language models and generative AI services before releasing them to the public. Apple Intelligence is expected to leverage AI models from Baidu and Alibaba. Meanwhile, HSBC upgraded AAPL stock to ‘Buy’ from ‘Hold,’ with a price target of $366, implying an upside of 10% from the stock’s last close. Apple has drawn increased attention in recent weeks after it announced hikes in prices for several products, including MacBooks, iPads, HomePods and Apple TV devices, fueling speculation that iPhone price increases could follow. Investors are also focused on the company's upcoming leadership change, with John Ternus set to succeed Tim Cook as CEO on Sept. 1. AAPL stock has risen nearly 23% so far in 2026, while retail sentiment on Stocktwits was ‘bullish’ at the time of writing. Shares of the psychedelics company surged to a yearly high of $7.22 after pharma giant Eli Lilly (LLY) confirmed its acquisition of AtaiBeckley. Eli Lilly said that it will acquire all outstanding ATAI shares for $6.75 per share in cash, with shareholders eligible for an additional up to $2.50 per share if certain development and regulatory milestones are achieved, bringing the deal's total potential value to $9.25 per share. The cash offer represents a 25.9% premium to ATAI's Wednesday closing price, while the maximum consideration implies a 72.6% premium. The acquisition is expected to close in the third quarter (Q3) of this year. ATAI stock is up more than 84% this year. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment was in the ‘extremely bullish’ territory at the time of writing. UNH stock touched a 52-week high of $461.62 in Thursday’s trading session after its second-quarter (Q2) earnings results blew past Wall Street estimates. The company posted revenue of $112.03 billion, up about 0.37% from $111.62 billion in the prior-year quarter. However, it beat Wall Street expectations of $110.9 billion, as per Fiscal.ai estimates. Meanwhile, net income came in at $5.48 billion, or $6.04 per share, compared with $3.41 billion, or $3.74 per share, in the same period a year ago. The health insurer now expects 2026 adjusted earnings of $19.50 to $20 per share, up from its prior outlook of more than $18.25 per share, while maintaining its revenue guidance of more than $439 billion for the year. The company attributed the better-than-expected results and higher full-year profit outlook to improved management of elevated medical costs and greater use of AI to streamline operations. Shares of AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) suffered their worst one-day drop in more than two years on Thursday after a $1 billion convertible-note raise rattled investors, but options veteran Jon Najarian said that the deal still represents “a pretty strong bet to the upside.” ASTS stock plunged 17% on Thursday to close at $55.01, marking its lowest closing level of the year. Najarian and his brother Pete Najarian broke down the financing and ASTS’ selloff in a Market Rebellion video posted on X. The brothers co-founded Market Rebellion, an options-focused market analysis platform, in 2016. AST SpaceMobile priced $1 billion of 1.625% convertible senior notes due in 2034, with an initial conversion price of $79.57 per share, which was about 20% above Wednesday’s close. Jon Najarian said that the notes give buyers the right, but not the obligation, to convert into ASTS shares at that price. While the 1.625% coupon is relatively low, he said the real appeal lies in the potential equity upside. “If the stock’s 200 bucks, you’re still exercising it at $79.57,” he said, calling the structure “a pretty strong bet to the upside.” The $200 figure was a hypothetical example, not a formal price target. Pete Najarian said that investors were focused on the risk that the notes could eventually convert into shares and dilute existing holders. “They’re concerned about dilution and all the rest of it,” he said, adding that the stock’s negative reaction was “understandable.” Still, he agreed the financing could support a valuable long-term opportunity. “I think this could be something into the future that could be pretty special, quite frankly,” he said. The brothers also stressed that ASTS remains a highly volatile trade. Implied volatility in the options was around 100%, according to Pete Najarian. “The implied volatility of this thing is not a joke,” he said. “Hell yes, this thing is volatile.” AST SpaceMobile said proceeds remaining after capped-call transactions may be used to secure additional access to orbit through “partnerships and/or acquisitions.” The company said the move could further vertically integrate its business and reduce reliance on third-party launch providers, although it currently has no agreement for any transaction. Satellite communications analyst Tim Farrar said that the language pointed to a potential acquisition. Potential names raised included United Launch Alliance, Firefly Aerospace, Relativity Space and Stoke Space. Farrar also said that AST may be trying to copy Rocket Lab’s vertically integrated model across launch and satellite infrastructure. “ASTS were outbid for Iridium, so it looks like they are now trying to copy Rocket Lab’s vertical integration play,” he said. The Najarians also suggested acquisitions may be part of the plan. “They’ve got some ideas with partnerships, acquisitions, all that kind of thing that people are excited about,” Jon Najarian said. “They just needed the capital,” he added. The financing comes as AST SpaceMobile continues expanding its BlueBird satellite network. BlueBird 10 recently deployed its communications array in low Earth orbit, while BlueBirds 8 and 9 are next. BlueBird 11 has arrived at Cape Canaveral, and BlueBirds 12 and 13 are being transported from Texas to Florida. AST said that the newer satellites are expected to deliver nearly twice the peak speeds of its first-generation spacecraft. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for ASTS slipped to ‘neutral’ from ‘bullish’ levels a day ago amid ‘high’ message volume. A Stocktwits poll with more than 2,000 votes showed retail traders largely remained bullish despite the selloff, with 49% saying they were "buying the dip," while 21% were waiting for a better entry, 19% planned to hold their positions, and just 11% said they were selling or trimming.
